Theme

Conversation, family & daily routines

annoy verb

also be annoyed, be annoyed at, annoying, this annoys me, annoyance

classical

Cic. Att. 1.12.3: quod tē molestē ferre certō sciō (Lewis & Short s.v. molestus)
Traupman 271

molestē ferre

ferō with the adverb; the thing in the accusative, or quod, or acc. and inf.

be annoyed at, take it ill

Other words

  • male habēre — annoy, trouble, harass

    habeō with the adverb; the person in the accusative · also used · classical · Caes. BC 1.63.2: agmen adversāriōrum male habēre (Lewis & Short s.v. habeō); Traupman 271

  • molestus esse (+ dat.) — be a nuisance, annoy

    also used · classical · Lewis & Short s.v. molestus

Examples

  • Hoc mē male habet.

    This annoys me.Traupman 271

See also trouble, disturb, angry.

SourcesLewis & Short: molestus · Lewis & Short: habeo

John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency (printed page numbers): p. 271.
